brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.requirement: Compact desk unit with a drawer
requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases (piece at 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1) plus a north-half base at 0,-1 carrying a classic drawer (drawer:0#0,-1#cut). Lock joints applied (3 joint bolts). check_build: meshClash clear, no rule errors.

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Mount spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 at the junction of the three full bases.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that mount spike (solid spikes refuse platforms, so the mount variant was used).

capOpenFaces refused with MESH_CLASH (hex-cap-edge-solid-m vs hex-drawer-frame-s, 4.49 mm) both with and without skipping the drawer-side faces. Left 15 open faces uncapped; check_build reports this as info only.

finish.summary: Built a small desk unit: three hex bases meeting at a corner with a mount spike carrying a small platform, plus a half base with a drawer on its south-facing cut side. Joints are locked. The house-rule cap pass conflicted with the drawer frame, so the open faces remain uncapped; the build is otherwise clear of mesh clashes.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
